chunks: 3. Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad Abu Sa'id al-Nisawi said: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Sughdi said in Marw that Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hakam al-Askari and his brother Mu'adh ibn Ya'qub both said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hanzali said: Abd Allah ibn Asim said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays said, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Rummani, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Salman al-Farisi, in a long tradition which mentions the arrival of the Catholicos to Medina with a hundred Christians after the death of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and his asking Abu Bakr about some matters which he did not answer, then he was directed to the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and asked him about them, and he answered. Among what he asked was that he said to him: Inform me about the Lord, where is He and where was He?

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: The Lord, Exalted be His Glory, is not described by place. He is as He was, and He was as He is. He was not in a place, nor did He remain from place to place, and place did not encompass Him. Rather, He has always been without limit and without quality. He said: You have spoken the truth. Inform me about the Lord, is He in this world or in the Hereafter?

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: Our Lord existed before the world, and He will exist forever. He is the Planner of the world, and the All-Knowing of the Hereafter. As for being encompassed by the world and the Hereafter, no. But He knows what is in the world and the Hereafter. He said: You have spoken the truth, may Allah have mercy on you.

Then he said: Inform me about your Lord, does He carry or is He carried? Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: Verily, our Lord, Exalted be His Glory, carries and is not carried. The Christian said: How is that? And we find in the Gospel (And the Throne of your Lord will be carried above them that day by eight).

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) replied: Verily, the angels carry the Throne. However, the Throne is not as you imagine, like the shape of a bed. Rather, it is something limited, created, and planned, and your Lord, Exalted and Mighty, is its owner. It is not that He is on it like one thing being on another. He commanded the angels to carry it, so they carry the Throne with what He has empowered them with. The Christian said: You have spoken the truth, may Allah have mercy on you. The tradition is long; we have taken from it what is needed, and I have transmitted it in full at the end of the book of Prophethood.

key_terms.بِلَا حَدٍّ وَلَا كَيْفٍ: Without limit and without quality (divine attributes)
key_terms.لَا يُوصَفُ بِمَكَانٍ: Not described by place (transcendence of space)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (AS) say about God's location and whether He is carried?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* records a profound theological dialogue where Imam Ali (AS) clarifies divine transcendence (*tanzih*) for a Christian Catholicos, addressing spatial location, temporal existence, and the nature of the Throne (*Arsh*). It serves as a key Shia exposition on God’s independence from physical containment, distinguishing between the Creator and the created entities that bear His throne, thereby refuting anthropomorphic conceptions of divinity.
